thymine as a nitrogenous base
phosphodiester bonds
nucleotides as monomers
questions.explain: One of the clearest DNA-RNA differences is thymine versus uracil.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Both DNA and RNA have sugar-phosphate backbones.
Correct. DNA uses thymine, whereas RNA usually uses uracil.
Incorrect. Both nucleic acids contain phosphodiester linkages.
Incorrect. Both are built from nucleotides.

questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a replication fork opening on a chromosome. Why is the lagging strand synthesized in fragments during DNA replication?
choices: Primase prevents continuous replication on both strands equally
RNA polymerase blocks the lagging strand
Helicase works only on one side of the replication fork
DNA polymerase can add nucleotides only in the 5′ to 3′ direction
questions.explain: Okazaki fragments arise because of strand antiparallelism and DNA polymerase directionality.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. The directionality of DNA polymerase is the core issue.
Incorrect. RNA polymerase is used for transcription, not as the main reason lagging fragments form.
Incorrect. Helicase unwinds both template strands at the fork.
Correct. Opposite strand orientation forces discontinuous synthesis away from the fork.

questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a replication fork opening on a chromosome. What is the main result of RNA splicing in eukaryotes?
choices: the ribosome attaches to the plasma membrane
amino acids are linked into a polypeptide
introns are removed and exons are joined together
DNA bases are changed to match the protein sequence
questions.explain: Splicing removes noncoding introns from pre-mRNA.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. That is unrelated to RNA processing.
Incorrect. That occurs during translation.
Correct. Splicing edits the primary transcript into mature mRNA.
Incorrect. Splicing alters RNA, not the DNA template.

questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a replication fork opening on a chromosome. Which mutation is most likely to have the greatest effect on the resulting polypeptide?
choices: a substitution in a stop codon of a nontranscribed pseudogene
a frameshift near the beginning of the coding region
a silent mutation in the third base of a codon
a mutation in an intron that is removed during splicing
questions.explain: Frameshifts early in coding regions often disrupt many amino acids and the stop position.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. A nontranscribed pseudogene would not typically affect the protein in question.
Correct. Early frameshifts alter many downstream codons.
Incorrect. Silent mutations often do not change the amino acid sequence.
Incorrect. Some intron mutations matter, but this option is usually less disruptive than an early frameshift.

Translation stops in all bacterial genes
RNA polymerase is permanently destroyed
questions.explain: The lac operon is induced when lactose inactivates the repressor.
choice_explanations: Correct. Inducer binding inactivates the repressor and permits transcription.

Incorrect. The lac operon affects a specific pathway.
Incorrect. The operon regulates transcription, not polymerase destruction.

Smaller fragments are converted into RNA during the run

Correct. Smaller fragments encounter less resistance as they migrate.
Incorrect. DNA fragments are negatively charged regardless of size.

questions.text: A student analyzes this experiment: semiconservative replication tested with labeled nucleotides. Cells grown first in heavy nitrogen and then in light nitrogen produce DNA of intermediate density after one round of replication. What does this support?

DNA replication is fully conservative
Mutations occur in every replication cycle
DNA replication is semiconservative
questions.explain: An intermediate-density band after one generation is classic evidence for semiconservative replication.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Density labeling experiments address strand inheritance, not overall macromolecule class.

Incorrect. The density result is about replication mechanism, not mutation frequency.
Correct. Each daughter DNA molecule contains one old strand and one new strand.

Lane 3 DNA is positively charged while lane 2 DNA is negative
Lane 3 must be RNA rather than DNA
questions.explain: Relative band position is used to infer fragment size.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Migration is driven mainly by size, not base composition alone.
Correct. Smaller fragments migrate farther through the gel.
Incorrect. DNA fragments are generally negatively charged due to their phosphate groups.
Incorrect. Position alone does not identify the nucleic acid type.

questions.text: A student analyzes this experiment: semiconservative replication tested with labeled nucleotides. A gene's mRNA level rises sharply after a transcription factor is activated. Which inference is most directly supported?
choices: The transcription factor likely promotes transcription of that gene
The gene's DNA sequence must have changed
Translation has stopped permanently
The ribosome has removed introns from the gene
questions.explain: Changes in mRNA abundance often reflect transcriptional regulation.
choice_explanations: Correct. A rise in mRNA after factor activation suggests positive regulation.
Incorrect. Expression changes do not require DNA sequence changes.
Incorrect. Higher mRNA does not imply translation stopped.
Incorrect. Introns are removed from RNA in the nucleus, not by ribosomes.

questions.text: A student analyzes this experiment: semiconservative replication tested with labeled nucleotides. Cells exposed to a mutagen show many insertion and deletion mutations. Which mutation type would be expected to increase most directly?
choices: chromosome-number changes only
crossing-over events
frameshift mutations
silent mutations only
questions.explain: Insertions and deletions are common causes of frameshifts.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Point-level insertions/deletions do not necessarily alter chromosome number.
Incorrect. Crossing over occurs during meiosis, not simply due to mutagen exposure in somatic cells.
Correct. Insertions and deletions can shift the reading frame.
Incorrect. Insertions and deletions often do more than cause silent changes.

Different cell types express different subsets of genes

Mutations never occur in normal cells

choices: Repair enzymes cause all mutations
DNA repair systems normally help maintain genomic stability
Mutations never occur in normal cells
DNA polymerase is unnecessary for replication
questions.explain: Repair pathways reduce the number of mutations that persist in DNA.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. The opposite is supported by the data.
Correct. Higher mutation rates in repair-deficient cells show the role of repair.
Incorrect. Normal cells still experience mutations; repair lowers the rate.
Incorrect. Replication still requires DNA polymerase.
